passage: Pulled the numbers from our gym's check-in app this month. Members who train before 7 a.m. have the lowest average body fat of any time slot, and it's not close. Early sessions just burn more fat, simple as that. Stuck on a plateau? Move your workouts to the morning and watch what happens. 5:30 crew, see you tomorrow.
cue: Early sessions just burn more fat, simple as that.
explanation: Brandon sees that early trainers are leaner and decides the early hour causes it. People who show up at 5:30 may differ in diet, routine or experience, so the link alone can't show the clock is doing the work.

whyNot.fal_post_hoc: Brandon isn't saying one event followed another; he's comparing groups of members and reading a correlation as cause.

title: Councillor says more cafés could make Millbrook wealthier
passage: Presenting a regional comparison on Tuesday, Councillor Dana Whitfield noted that the five towns with the most independent coffee shops per resident also have the highest median household incomes. She proposed rent relief to attract new cafés, arguing that more coffee shops would help lift local wages.
cue: arguing that more coffee shops would help lift local wages
explanation: Whitfield treats the link between cafés and incomes as if cafés create wealth. The arrow may point the other way: towns where people already earn more can support more coffee shops.

whyNot.fal_texas_sharpshooter: She didn't sift data for a lucky cluster; she took a plain correlation across towns and assumed which way the cause runs.

title: Proposal: Quillmoor for every team
passage: Hi all, quick follow-up on last quarter. The five teams that chose to adopt Quillmoor finished about 30% more work requests per person than the teams that stayed on spreadsheets. Licenses are cheap and setup takes an afternoon. Given the gap, I'm confident the tool is what's driving the extra output, so I'd like to make it mandatory from September. Comments welcome before Friday.
cue: I'm confident the tool is what's driving the extra output
explanation: Gareth credits the tool for the gap, but teams chose whether to adopt it. Teams eager to try new tools may already have been the faster ones, so the comparison can't show the tool caused the difference.

whyNot.fal_post_hoc: There's no before-and-after story here; Gareth compares adopters with non-adopters and treats that group difference as the tool's doing.

source: Principal Ortega · Westfield High parent evening
passage: We looked closely at last year's report cards, and one pattern stood out: students who sat in the first two rows averaged almost a full letter grade higher than students at the back. Our teachers work hard to reach every row, and they'll keep doing that. But starting this term, we'll seat students who are struggling up front so they get the same boost.
cue: we'll seat students who are struggling up front so they get the same boost
explanation: Principal Ortega assumes the front row produces the higher grades. Students who are already keen often choose to sit up front, so moving others there may not deliver the same 'boost'.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: A full year of report cards is a decent sample; the problem is assuming the seat causes the grades when keen students may simply pick the front.

title: Green tea drinkers catch fewer colds, survey of 12,000 finds
passage: Adults who drank at least two cups of green tea a day reported 20% fewer colds over the winter than those who drank none, even after researchers adjusted for age and smoking. Lead author Dr. Mirela Sandu said the result shows compounds in the tea strengthen the immune system, and recommended a daily cup through flu season.
cue: the result shows compounds in the tea strengthen the immune system
explanation: Dr. Sandu moves from an association to a cause. Daily tea drinkers may also exercise more, eat differently or report symptoms differently, and adjusting for age and smoking doesn't rule those out.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: With 12,000 people, sample size isn't the issue; the leap is from an adjusted correlation to the tea itself doing the protecting.

passage:
Imani: Went through my shop stats last night. Listings with 8+ photos sell about twice as often as the ones with 3 or 4.
Theo: makes sense, people want to see what they're buying
Imani: Right?? So I'm reshooting all my cheap listings with 8 photos each. That should double their sales.
Theo: worth a weekend for sure
cue: I'm reshooting all my cheap listings with 8 photos each. That should double their sales.
explanation: Imani assumes the extra photos caused the extra sales. The listings she photographed most may be her best items, which sell well anyway, so adding photos to cheaper ones may not double anything.

whyNot.fal_texas_sharpshooter: Imani didn't hunt through her data for a lucky cluster; she noticed one plain pattern and assumed photos are what drive it.

source: Dr. Leila Haddad, Brookside Family Clinic
title: Results of our reminder-text pilot
passage: Hi everyone, here are the pilot results. For three months, patients booking appointments were randomly assigned to get a text reminder the day before or no reminder. The no-show rate was 8% with texts and 14% without, across about 1,900 appointments. Since the groups were split by chance, the texts are the likely reason for the drop, so I suggest we keep them.
cue: randomly assigned to get a text reminder the day before or no reminder
explanation: Dr. Haddad's groups were split at random, so other differences between patients should even out. That makes the reminders a fair explanation for the lower no-show rate.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: Random assignment reduces systematic differences between groups, so the results support a causal explanation. Chance variation and study limitations remain possible.

title: Asthma ER visits fell along electric bus routes, study finds
passage: After Dunmore replaced its diesel buses with electric ones in 2024, asthma-related ER visits fell 11% the next year, while neighboring Carver, which kept its diesel fleet, saw no change. The drop was largest in blocks along bus routes. Researchers say the pattern points to cleaner air from the new buses as a likely contributor.
cue: while neighboring Carver, which kept its diesel fleet, saw no change
explanation: The researchers don't rely on timing or one correlation alone. A similar town without the change acts as a comparison, and the effect is strongest nearest the buses, so 'likely contributor' is a fair conclusion.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: A comparison town plus a stronger effect near the routes helps rule out other explanations, and the claim is suitably modest.
